findings.title: Member add/remove routes are declared at collection scope, so the URLs the client calls don't exist
findings.body: The `delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"` and `put "members" => "groups#add_members"` lines are placed directly inside the `resources :groups` block (not inside a `member do ... end` block), so they generate the collection routes `/admin/groups/members` with no `:id` segment. However, the frontend calls `/admin/groups/<group_id>/members.json` (see `Discourse.Group#addMembers`/`#removeMember` in app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js), and the controller actions do `params.require(:group_id)`. Those requests will 404 (no route matches `/admin/groups/1/members`), making both adding and removing group members from the admin UI completely non-functional. The routes need to be wrapped in `member do ... end` (or declared as `put "/groups/:id/members"`).

findings.title: Automatic-group removal test uses the wrong HTTP verb (PUT instead of DELETE)
findings.body: The test "cannot remove members from automatic groups" issues `xhr :put, :remove_member, group_id: 1, user_id: 42`, but the route for remove_member is a DELETE (`delete "members" => "groups#remove_member"`). Once the route is correctly scoped as a member route, this test will fail with a routing error (or hit nothing) instead of asserting the 422 automatic-group behavior. It should be `xhr :delete, :remove_member, ...` to match the other remove_member test and the actual route verb.

findings.title: `automatic` is not in scope in the member item view, so remove links are shown for automatic groups
findings.body: The group_member template uses `{{#unless automatic}}` to hide the remove link, but this template is rendered in the context of the `group-member` item view whose content is the individual member (a Discourse.User), not the group. `automatic` is not a property of a user, so it evaluates as falsy and the remove link is rendered for every member — including members of automatic groups. Clicking it fires `removeMember`, which the server rejects with 422 ("can not modify automatic"), producing a silently failing/confusing action with no user-facing error handling (there is no failure handler on `removeMember` in the model or controller).

findings.title: totalPages is off by one when user_count is an exact multiple of limit
findings.body: `totalPages` computes `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1`. When user_count is an exact multiple of limit (e.g. 50 members with limit 50, or 100 with limit 50), this yields one page too many (2 pages for 50 members). The `showingLast` computed then never becomes true on the real last page, so the "next" arrow stays enabled and clicking it fetches an empty member page, showing an empty list while claiming page 2/2. The calculation should use `Math.ceil(user_count / limit)`.

findings.title: add_members silently ignores non-existent usernames and reports success
findings.body: `add_members` iterates the submitted usernames and only adds users found via `User.find_by_username`, but if a username doesn't match any user it is silently skipped and the endpoint still returns `success_json`. The admin UI then reloads the member list and gives the operator no indication that some (or all) of the requested members were not added — typos appear to succeed. The endpoint should report which usernames could not be found so the client can surface an error.

findings.title: create drops the alias_level parameter the client sends
findings.body: The new `Discourse.Group#create` (app/assets/javascripts/discourse/models/group.js) posts `asJSON()` which includes `alias_level`, but the server's `create` action only assigns `name` and `visible`; `alias_level` is never read. A newly created group therefore always gets the default alias level regardless of what the admin selected in the form, and the value is only applied later if the admin saves again. `group.alias_level = params[:alias_level].to_i if params[:alias_level].present?` should also be applied in `create`.

findings.title: members endpoint accepts an unbounded limit parameter
findings.body: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` is passed straight into `group.users.limit(limit)` with no maximum cap and no guard against nonsense values. Any client (this is a public, non-admin endpoint) can request `/groups/<name>/members.json?limit=1000000` and force serialization of the group's entire membership in one request, which on large groups (e.g. trust_level_0) is an expensive query and serialization. A sane cap such as `[limit, 1000].min` (and flooring at 0) should be enforced.
